sentences.text: Chaoyangsaurus was a small member of the Ceratopsia, a group of dinosaurs known as "horned faces". It possessed light legs, a slender body, a very short and undeveloped bony frill, a small beak, and no horns.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — comes from the Tuchengzi Formation and includes a partial skeleton with the lower skull, braincase, lower jaws, seven neck vertebrae, a right shoulder blade, and a right humerus.
Its skull measures fourteen centimeters in length, and five specific anatomical traits were identified as unique autapomorphies distinguishing it from other dinosaurs.
Due to the scarcity of bones found, the exact length, height, and weight of Chaoyangsaurus remain unknown.
Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Chaoyangsaurus was about 1 meter long and weighed 6 kilograms.
This dinosaur had a very short and undeveloped bony frill, a feature not seen in many later relatives.
The remains of Chaoyangsaurus were discovered in 1976 by Cheng Zhengwu at Ershijiazi in Liaoning Province, China.
Chaoyangsaurus did not receive an official scientific name until 1999.
Chaoyangsaurus was primarily a herbivore, feeding on plants such as ferns, cycads, and conifers that were dominant in its era.

Chaoyangsaurus lived before Protoceratops and Psittacosaurus, which are considered some of the earliest members of the Ceratopsia family. In 2006, Zhao and colleagues defined Chaoyangsauridae as the most basal clade within the Ceratopsia.
Chaoyangsaurus has been classified in various groups over time, including Chaoyoungosauroidea, Psittacosauridae, and finally confirmed in Chaoyangosauridae.
The holotype specimen of Chaoyangsaurus comes from the Tuchengzi Formation, dated to the late Tithonian stage.
It is debated whether Chaoyangsaurus falls outside or inside the Neoceratopia clade.
